name: PARACETAMOL 250 MG / ACETYLSALICALIC ACID 250 MG / CAFFEINE 65 MG 24 TABLETS
description: Yes, it is possible to take paracetamol and acetylsalicylic acid (ASA, commonly known as aspirin) together, and they are often combined in over-the-counter products for greater pain relief. Unlike aspirin and other NSAIDs (such as ibuprofen), paracetamol works differently, and combining them does not increase the risk of gastrointestinal side effects. Combination Products Some products combine both medications, often with caffeine, to treat headaches and migraines. If discomfort persists, consult your doctor.
